title: Complete the interpreter mocks that produce optimizer feedback
motivation: The FIŘ interpreter runs the warmup and records the feedback that the optimizer speculates on. It failed on bounce, list_for, list_while, matrix_for and promise_reflect, because its mocks of R builtins lacked operations that these benchmarks use. So these benchmarks timed only the unspeculated baseline, with a regular `mkenv` and frame loads and stores of every variable. promise_reflect still fails after this range, because it also needs a `tryCatch` mock.
solution: `fir/interpret/internal/Builtins.java` extends the mocks. The generic `[[<-` and `[<-` grow a vector past its end, `[`, `[[`, `[<-` and `[[<-` accept name subscripts, and arithmetic, comparison, `abs` and `as.logical` keep or drop names like GNU-R. `matrix` and row-and-column subscripts work, with `InternalInterpreter#registerUnmatchedExternal` for a dynamic `x[[i, j]] <- v`. `environment()` and `ls` of a frame work, including the vendored R's reflection marker. Also in this range: `[[` reads an absent list name as `NULL`, and `ls` only accepts names that sort the same in the C and UTF-8 collations.

files.repo-map.md: Adds entries for the five new `mod_*` examples.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: Adds subscript growth, name subscripts, name propagation in arithmetic, `matrix`, matrix subscripts, `environment()` and `ls` to the interpreter mocks.
Adds `registerUnmatchedExternal`, which runs a mock for a dynamic call whose arguments do not match the function's parameters.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: New example: arithmetic, comparison, unary minus and `abs` of named vectors, to check which names the result keeps.
New example: `ls` of frames from `environment()`, with hidden names and the vendored R's reflection marker.
New example: `matrix` with missing or recycled arguments, and `[[`, `[`, `[[<-`, `[<-` with a row and column.
New example: `[[<-` and `[<-` past the end of lists and of integer, real and named string vectors.
New example: `[`, `[[`, `[<-` and `[[<-` with present, absent and appended name subscripts.
